messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: vectorized probability functions
parts:
Taking Matt's insights to heart, I've been looking
more closely at what we need to do to vectorize
probability functions.

So far, the only instance is the sampled values for a normal:

normal_log(std::vector<T_y>& ys, T_loc& mu, T_scale& sigma);

What I'd like to do is generalize the ys argument to
Eigen vectors and matrices (Daniel generalized Eigen's
interfaces to make this possible using their nifty
plugin architecture). But the problem is that if I template
out the first arg fully, I get an ambiguity with the
non-vectorized normal_log function.

normal_log(T_y& ys, T_loc& mu, T_scale& sigma);

Would anyone mind if I changed the name of the vectorized
one to either:

normals_log OR normal_vec_log

Any preferences? Something else?

Remembering an earlier lesson of Matt's on the symmetry
of mu and y in y ~ Normal(mu,sigma), we could
get away (at least for now) with only vectorizing the
ys parameter. Consider:

for (n in 1:N)
ys[n] ~ normal(mus[n],sigma);

which we could vectorize in this form:

(y - mu) ~ normal(0,sigma);

It's ugly, but it will produce the same result without
needing to vectorize the location params.

- Bob

On 5/30/12 6:30 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Wednesday, May 30, 2012 6:11:09 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:

> Is it possible to change this definition to
>
> normal_log(scalar& ys, T_loc& mu, T_scale& sigma)
>
> using the typedef in src/stan/math/matrix.hpp ?

And that scalar typedef is local to the EigenType struct.
Once we have the vector/matrix type, it's easy to
extract the scalar type from it.

No -- we don't know what the type of ys will be.
It could be vector<T> or Matrix<T,R,C> for R=1,C=-1,
R=-1,C=1, or R=1,C=1.

In general, the problem with using EigenType<T> is that
it won't allow type inference through it (at least not
that I've figured out how to do). So it's great when you
know what T is, but if you don't, not so much.

> Would anyone mind if I changed the name of the vectorized
> one to either:
>
> normals_log OR normal_vec_log
>
> Any preferences? Something else?
>
>
> If that is the only way to do it, okay.
I don't see another way to do it.

> But in general, having all these weird variations on function names is
> disturbing to me.

Some would argue that overloading is disturbing!
I don't mind one way or the other.

> Remembering an earlier lesson of Matt's on the symmetry
> of mu and y in y ~ Normal(mu,sigma), we could
> get away (at least for now) with only vectorizing the
> ys parameter. Consider:
>
> for (n in 1:N)
> ys[n] ~ normal(mus[n],sigma);
>
> which we could vectorize in this form:
>
> (y - mu) ~ normal(0,sigma);
>
> It's ugly, but it will produce the same result without
> needing to vectorize the location params.
>
>
> Last resort, IMO.

I'm thinking more of a first resort, because it'll be
a while before we can get all the vectorized probability
functions implemented. Especially if we're going to
push through good derivative calc classes.

- Bob
